## Module to write
path: ServerScriptService/PadFeedbackService.luau
purpose: Feature: Visual and feel pass (art, juice, readability; no gameplay rules change): For the visible buy pad, pulse a green Highlight or neon glow and its price tag while the owner's Cash >= cost, and stop it when not affordable or after a buy. Count it in a 'highlights' census counter. When a player touches a pad with too little cash, flash the pad red, play an error buzz and show a short 'Need $N' toast without deducting cash. Hook into UpgradeService and UpgradeFx, and increment a pad_denied counter. -- Server module (required by UpgradeService, no auto-boot needed beyond lazy Init on first require). Creates the ReplicatedStorage RemoteEvent 'PadFeedback'. API: Register(pad: BasePart, owner: Player, cost: number), which records the visible pad and its owner and refreshes affordability; Unregister(pad), called when the pad is bought or hidden, which removes its Highlight and clears the 'Affordable' attribute; Denied(player, pad, cost), called on an insufficient-cash touch, which is debounced per player/pad at about 1s, fires PadFeedback:FireClient(player, 'denied', pad, cost) and bumps 'pad_denied'. It watches each owner's leaderstats Cash.Changed plus a 0.5s heartbeat check. While Cash >= cost for a registered pad it sets pad attribute Affordable=true and creates or enables a green Highlight (named 'AffordHighlight', FillColor green, FillTransparency 0.6, OutlineColor white, Adornee pad), bumping 'highlights' once each time a highlight is activated. When Cash < cost, or after Unregister or the owner leaving, it sets Affordable=false and disables or destroys the Highlight. It never changes Cash or purchase rules. It uses ForgeTelemetry and cleans up on PlayerRemoving. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: highlights, pad_denied.
depends: ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau

### ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau
```luau
--!strict
-- ForgeTelemetry: tiny counter API for generated games. ForgeProbe reports these counters.
--
--   local ForgeTelemetry = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").ForgeTelemetry)
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("coins_collected")      -- +1
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("damage_dealt", 25)     -- +25
--   ForgeTelemetry.get()                          -- { coins_collected = 1, damage_dealt = 25 }
--
-- Counters live as number attributes on ServerStorage.ForgeCounters (a Folder), so every VM in the
-- server (game scripts, ForgeProbe, execute_luau) sees the same values. Server only: on the client
-- count() is a no-op and get() returns {}.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local FOLDER_NAME = "ForgeCounters"

local ForgeTelemetry = {}

local function folder(): Instance?
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return nil
	end
	local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
	local f = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		f = Instance.new("Folder")
		f.Name = FOLDER_NAME
		f.Parent = ServerStorage
	end
	return f
end

-- Attribute names: letters, digits and underscores, max 100 chars, may not start with "RBX".
local function key(name: string): string
	local k = string.gsub(tostring(name), "[^%w_]", "_")
	if k == "" then
		k = "_"
	end
	if string.sub(k, 1, 3) == "RBX" then
		k = "_" .. k
	end
	return string.sub(k, 1, 100)
end

function ForgeTelemetry.count(name: string, n: number?)
	local f = folder()
	if not f then
		return
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		local k = key(name)
		local cur = f:GetAttribute(k)
		local add = tonumber(n) or 1
		f:SetAttribute(k, (if type(cur) == "number" then cur else 0) + add)
	end)
	if not ok then
		-- telemetry must never break the game
		return
	end
end

function ForgeTelemetry.get(): { [string]: number }
	local out: { [string]: number } = {}
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return out
	end
	local f = game:GetService("ServerStorage"):FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		return out
	end
	for k, v in f:GetAttributes() do
		if type(v) == "number" then
			out[k] = v
		end
	end
	return out
end

return ForgeTelemetry

```

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Also keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price, so the shop and later upgrades get exercised.
- Do not give starting cash equal to the first upgrade's price. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must still be easy to find and reach: guide the player to the first pad with a visible beam or arrow.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds (about 3-5s, not 20s), and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly. Keep the spec's auto-claim delay and the tested window consistent so the plaza state can still be observed before the claim.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. Make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0). If the census shows beams = 0, the guide is invisible: fix the beam creation (attachments, parenting, target lookup), not just its config.
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. Big moments deserve stronger feedback than routine ones: camera shake, a shockwave ring, or a larger popup. Mark milestones such as the first cube, the first affordable upgrade and tier-ups with a distinct presentation.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Luau parses a line that starts with `(` after a call or expression as a continuation, giving "Ambiguous syntax". Never start a statement with a parenthesis. Assign to a local first, or end the previous statement with `;`.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Bump an effect counter (sound, burst, popup) where the effect is really created, not where the remote is fired. If the counter is high but the census shows 0 sounds or bursts, the effects are not real or are destroyed before they are counted. Fix the effect, don't trust the counter.

## UI kit (house style for all UI: paste the snippets you use, Theme first, and adapt; plain Luau, not modules)
- Chunky text: every label gets a dark UIStroke (2.5-4 px). LuckiestGuy for titles/numbers, FredokaOne for body. Never default or thin fonts.
- One palette everywhere: yellow Primary = main action, green Good = affordable/claim, red Bad = close/can't, blue Info = secondary, dark Ink outlines.
- Depth: UICorner 12-18 px, UIStroke border, light-top UIGradient fill, hard drop shadow 4-6 px below.
- Everything moves: appear with a Back-eased UIScale pop (0 -> 1), react with a punch (1.2 -> 1), press squish to 0.9. Tween UIScale, not Size; 0.1-0.4 s, never linear.
- Numbers tick up and pop on change, big values short ("12.5K"); gains flash green, losses red.
- Every action gives feedback: toast, floating "+N" or reward popup. Max 3 toasts.
- Mobile first: 1280x720 offsets under a viewport UIScale (`Theme.screen`), safe insets, buttons >= 44 px, nothing key in the top-left (Roblox menu).
- HUD hugs the edges, centre stays clear; windows open over a dim backdrop with a close X.
- World prices on BillboardGuis: green when affordable, red when not.
- UI is built in code with Instance.new, no image asset ids (emoji/letters for icons), ResetOnSpawn = false.

```luau
--!strict
-- PadFeedbackService: affordability glow + denied feedback for buy pads. Never touches Cash or purchase rules.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Telemetry = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeTelemetry"))

local GREEN = Color3.fromRGB(70, 255, 120)
local RED = Color3.fromRGB(255, 60, 60)
local DENY_DEBOUNCE = 1
local CHECK_INTERVAL = 0.5

type Entry = {
	owner: Player,
	cost: number,
	highlight: Highlight?,
	tween: Tween?,
	active: boolean,
	ancestryConn: RBXScriptConnection?,
	tagOrig: { [TextLabel]: Color3 },
	flashing: boolean,
}

local PadFeedback = {}

local entries: { [BasePart]: Entry } = {}
local cashConns: { [Player]: RBXScriptConnection } = {}
local deniedAt: { [Player]: { [BasePart]: number } } = {}
local remote: RemoteEvent

local function getCash(player: Player): number?
	local ls = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	if not ls then
		return nil
	end
	local cash = ls:FindFirstChild("Cash")
	if cash and (cash:IsA("IntValue") or cash:IsA("NumberValue")) then
		return cash.Value
	end
	return nil
end

local function tagLabels(pad: BasePart): { TextLabel }
	local out = {}
	local roots: { Instance } = { pad }
	if pad.Parent and pad.Parent:IsA("Model") then
		table.insert(roots, pad.Parent)
	end
	for _, root in roots do
		for _, d in root:GetDescendants() do
			if d:IsA("TextLabel") and d:FindFirstAncestorWhichIsA("BillboardGui") then
				table.insert(out, d)
			end
		end
		if #out > 0 then
			break
		end
	end
	return out
end

local function deactivate(pad: BasePart, e: Entry)
	if e.tween then
		e.tween:Cancel()
		e.tween = nil
	end
	if e.highlight then
		e.highlight:Destroy()
		e.highlight = nil
	end
	for label, col in e.tagOrig do
		if label.Parent then
			label.TextColor3 = col
		end
	end
	e.tagOrig = {}
	e.active = false
	if pad.Parent then
		pad:SetAttribute("Affordable", false)
	end
end

local function activate(pad: BasePart, e: Entry)
	e.active = true
	pad:SetAttribute("Affordable", true)
	local h = Instance.new("Highlight")
	h.Name = "AffordHighlight"
	h.FillColor = GREEN
	h.FillTransparency = 0.6
	h.OutlineColor = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	h.OutlineTransparency = 0
	h.DepthMode = Enum.HighlightDepthMode.AlwaysOnTop
	h.Adornee = pad
	h.Enabled = true
	h.Parent = pad
	e.highlight = h
	local tw = TweenService:Create(h, TweenInfo.new(0.6, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut, -1, true), {
		FillTransparency = 0.85,
	})
	tw:Play()
	e.tween = tw
	for _, label in tagLabels(pad) do
		e.tagOrig[label] = label.TextColor3
		label.TextColor3 = GREEN
	end
	Telemetry.count("highlights", 1)
end

local function refresh(pad: BasePart)
	local e = entries[pad]
	if not e then
		return
	end
	local cash = getCash(e.owner)
	local affordable = cash ~= nil and cash >= e.cost
	if affordable and not e.active then
		activate(pad, e)
	elseif not affordable and e.active then
		deactivate(pad, e)
	end
end

local function watchCash(player: Player)
	if cashConns[player] then
		return
	end
	local ls = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	local cash = ls and ls:FindFirstChild("Cash")
	if cash and cash:IsA("ValueBase") then
		cashConns[player] = (cash :: any).Changed:Connect(function()
			for pad, e in entries do
				if e.owner == player then
					refresh(pad)
				end
			end
		end)
	end
end

function PadFeedback.Unregister(pad: BasePart)
	local e = entries[pad]
	if not e then
		return
	end
	entries[pad] = nil
	if e.ancestryConn then
		e.ancestryConn:Disconnect()
	end
	deactivate(pad, e)
end

function PadFeedback.Register(pad: BasePart, owner: Player, cost: number)
	if typeof(pad) ~= "Instance" or not pad:IsA("BasePart") then
		return
	end
	if typeof(owner) ~= "Instance" or not owner:IsA("Player") or type(cost) ~= "number" then
		return
	end
	local e = entries[pad]
	if e then
		e.owner = owner
		e.cost = cost
	else
		local newEntry: Entry = {
			owner = owner,
			cost = cost,
			highlight = nil,
			tween = nil,
			active = false,
			ancestryConn = nil,
			tagOrig = {},
			flashing = false,
		}
		newEntry.ancestryConn = pad.AncestryChanged:Connect(function(_, parent)
			if parent == nil then
				PadFeedback.Unregister(pad)
			end
		end)
		entries[pad] = newEntry
		pad:SetAttribute("Affordable", false)
	end
	watchCash(owner)
	refresh(pad)
end

function PadFeedback.Denied(player: Player, pad: BasePart, cost: number)
	if typeof(player) ~= "Instance" or not player:IsA("Player") then
		return
	end
	if typeof(pad) ~= "Instance" or not pad:IsA("BasePart") then
		return
	end
	local c = if type(cost) == "number" then cost else 0
	local perPlayer = deniedAt[player]
	if not perPlayer then
		perPlayer = {}
		deniedAt[player] = perPlayer
	end
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = perPlayer[pad]
	if last and now - last < DENY_DEBOUNCE then
		return
	end
	perPlayer[pad] = now
	Telemetry.count("pad_denied", 1)
	remote:FireClient(player, "denied", pad, c)

	-- server-side red flash so feedback exists even without client help
	local e = entries[pad]
	if not (e and e.flashing) then
		if e then
			e.flashing = true
		end
		local original = pad.Color
		pad.Color = RED
		task.delay(0.35, function()
			if pad.Parent then
				pad.Color = original
			end
			if e then
				e.flashing = false
			end
		end)
	end
end

local function onPlayerRemoving(player: Player)
	for pad, e in entries do
		if e.owner == player then
			PadFeedback.Unregister(pad)
		end
	end
	local conn = cashConns[player]
	if conn then
		conn:Disconnect()
		cashConns[player] = nil
	end
	deniedAt[player] = nil
end

local function init()
	local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("PadFeedback")
	if existing and existing:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
		remote = existing
	else
		remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
		remote.Name = "PadFeedback"
		remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	end
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(onPlayerRemoving)
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(CHECK_INTERVAL)
			for pad, e in entries do
				watchCash(e.owner)
				refresh(pad)
			end
		end
	end)
end

init()

return PadFeedback
```
